items.title: Seek directly through thread history
items.summary: Schema v28 replaces the old single-column reply index with (thread_root_id, id), speeding sparse old-thread tail reads.
items.before: A thread tail without a cursor could scan a channel's unrelated newer messages and sort before finding the requested replies.
items.after: The SQLite plan seeks the requested thread's ordered range directly; the old index is replaced rather than retained alongside a duplicate.
items.mechanism: The composite index matches both the equality filter and message-order range used by thread pages and has-more probes.

evidence.label: OPT-10 measured index decision and costs

metrics.label: Old thread newest page, 200k messages, warm p50
Old thread newest page, warm p95

limits: Historical Linux Xeon/Node 24.21 fixture with 30 warm HTTP samples; not a current installation capacity claim.
Cursor-bounded pages were already fast and showed no comparable gain. Extra index space/build/write cost is part of the decision.

items.title: Render only rows whose displayed entities changed
items.summary: Message rows subscribe to the author, mentioned/reacting users, referenced channels and primitive self identity/role instead of entire maps.
items.before: An unrelated user's profile edit, other-channel membership or own status change rendered all 300 loaded rows.
items.after: Unrelated changes render zero rows; renaming an author updates only rows that show that author, while permission changes still update the affected controls.
items.mechanism: Stable derived entity selectors preserve object references while unchanged maps/entries remain semantically equal.

evidence.label: OPT-05 production React/jsdom measurements and selector cost

metrics.label: Rows rendered for an unrelated profile change
Rows rendered when author of 60 rows is renamed

limits: Historical React production build under jsdom measures React work without real layout/paint.
Selectors add small per-event work and the change added about 1 kB to that historical entry.

items.title: Start unread mention work from the mentions index
items.summary: Schema v31 materializes message-to-recipient mention membership instead of scanning every channel message for each account's count.
items.before: Every recount rechecked message text across joined channels; a room-wide mention repeated that work for every member.
items.after: Counts and Activity start from the account's direct or room-wide mention candidates, then apply the shared channel/thread read rule.
items.mechanism: Store updates message_mentions transactionally on create/edit/delete; retention cascades its rows. The migration parses existing text under the same mention rules.

evidence.label: OPT-12 count, Activity, send and database measurements

limits: Historical seeded measurements; text scanning/index maintenance raises send work and slightly increases database size.
Thread unread semantics remain authoritative; older clients may not understand later unreadHold additions.

items.title: Build snapshots with batched managers and sparse presence
items.summary: Schema v34 and batched list reads remove two handshake costs that scaled with the account/member count.
items.before: The channel list made one manager/member query per channel; manager lookups scanned ordinary members. Presence reloaded all users to mark them offline.
items.after: A partial manager index and two shared reads build visible channel metadata; the presence map names only online accounts.
items.mechanism: Only is_manager=1 membership rows enter the new index. Missing presence already means offline in the client, and snapshots replace the map rather than merge stale online entries.

evidence.label: OPT-13 component, handshake, size and herd measurements

limits: Historical workload and host; the complete users list still dominates large snapshots.
Lean account bootstrap/paged People would require a further protocol decision, not just this query optimization.

items.title: Keep common-word search bounded and sparse/name search selective
items.summary: Two delivered search changes choose the appropriate query shape while preserving exact page content and access filters.
items.before: A common word required resolving, joining and sorting every matching message for one page; filename eligibility was repeatedly evaluated in sparse queries.
items.after: Common full-text terms use a newest-first scoped window with exact fallback; sparse terms combine bounded text matches and filename rowids once.
items.mechanism: A match count capped at 5,001 selects the path. Terms over the 5,000 threshold keep a 20,000-message window; the F13 sparse branch uses full-text rows UNION ALL file-message rows, then shared hydration/filtering.

evidence.label: F13 selective rewrite, exactness matrix and rejected alternatives
Before query timing and page hashes
After query timing and identical page hashes

limits: The two comparisons use different historical revisions; their gains must not be added.
Rare/hidden/in-channel queries can pay small admission overhead. Blanket message-ID UNION and separate filename-statement experiments were rejected.
No rare-author/date index was rolled out from research candidates; benchmark promises are limited to tested fixtures.

items.title: Move first-use-only screens and dialogs out of the entry
items.summary: Join, profile and friends screens join other deferred dialogs/panels as lazy modules.
items.before: Returning signed-in readers downloaded code for first-use screens that they did not need during initial chat rendering.
items.after: Those modules load on use, restoring measured historical headroom under the 500 kB entry guard.
items.mechanism: React lazy imports and Suspense boundaries split code while keeping the shared application route behavior and chunk-failure handling.

evidence.label: Later current implementation bundle identities and budgets

metrics.label: Historical web entry after first-use split

limits: This is a historical bundle-byte comparison, not a measured startup improvement.
Later features consume the restored headroom: the N01–N12 build recorded web 496,783 and desktop 499,463 bytes against 500,000.

items.title: Preserve unchanged thread and link-context references
items.summary: Client cache and hosting/link context updates avoid rebuilding unrelated visible content.
items.before: An unrelated channel message could slice/replace every cached thread, and a connected-count/backup-status update could invalidate shared message-link context.
items.after: Only relevant threads/pages and semantically changed link fields receive new references.
items.mechanism: Route live events by message/root ownership; derive provider values from address-relevant fields rather than the entire hosting snapshot.
limits: Correct reference preservation is covered; the historical Profiler comparison was not rerun in the later follow-up review.
In-flight history still buffers ordered events under the snapshot watermark rules.

items.title: Share equivalent history requests and coalesce Activity refreshes
items.summary: Equivalent tail/older/thread/newer loads share a transfer, and automatic Activity updates collapse into bounded work.
items.before: Repeated equivalent paging started duplicate requests and aborted one; a mention burst repeatedly blanked/refetched Activity.
items.after: Equivalent cursor/window callers settle from one request, replaced windows cancel, and Activity remains visible until the new answer arrives.
items.mechanism: Each history run has AbortController plus request/window identity; CoalescedLoader debounces automatic changes for 250 ms and permits at most one follow-up load while active. Explicit filter/page/Refresh loads remain immediate.

metrics.label: Requests for the recorded ten-change Activity burst

limits: This records request-count and visible-state controls, not an end-to-end latency benchmark.
Changed cursors/windows, real network failures, live replay, ordering and destruction retain their existing semantics.

items.title: Bound transient private app answers
items.summary: Private command replies retained by the client have count and text budgets, with replacement by repeated IDs.
items.before: Long sessions could accumulate arbitrarily many or large private answers outside bounded durable history.
items.after: The client keeps bounded transient answers and replaces an existing answer of the same identity rather than accumulating duplicates.
items.mechanism: Admission/eviction operates on the private-answer collection, preserving durable workspace messages and the active visible reply behavior.
limits: The recorded frame/control result is one fixture, not the configured limit or a whole-process memory guarantee.
Screen-reader/physical scrolling acceptance remains separate.

items.title: Avoid offline/repeated publication authorization and recount work
items.summary: Fan-out shares short-lived authorization/audience work inside a committed synchronous publication batch.
items.before: Private deletion rebuilt a channel's audience per event even with no readers; multiple devices of the same session repeated the same session lookup.
items.after: Offline private batches read no audience, and online batches share one channel read while still sending every durable deletion frame.
items.mechanism: Gateway visits connected byUser recipients, memoizes session checks only within the publication and server batches replaceable recounts; it does not introduce long-lived authorization cache.

metrics.label: Two-reader audience reads for same batch

limits: Single Linux host; actual timing depends on membership, readers and storage.
Membership/revocation checks remain authoritative; failed authorization closes the affected session and sends no dependent frame.

items.title: Share integration eligibility and payload construction per event
items.summary: One bot with many subscriptions reuses the same bot/channel eligibility and common event envelope.
items.before: One event with 100 subscriptions repeated identical membership, workspace metadata and JSON serialization work 100 times.
items.after: Distinct subscriptions still get their own durable delivery rows, but shared checks/read/body construction run once.
items.mechanism: Group event preparation by bot/channel within the event, retain per-subscription filtering/admission/redaction, then insert the distinct delivery jobs.
limits: No clear timing change at one or ten subscriptions; row writes remain necessary.
Single-host measured result is not a general integration capacity claim.

items.title: Keep heavy backup SQL off main and keep workers dependency-light
items.summary: Desktop backup/verify/inventory/restore workers import only the focused backup module.
items.before: Full server-barrel imports pulled networking dependencies into jobs that only needed database/filesystem backup work.
items.after: The emitted focused worker was verified at 44,577 bytes and packaged backup/restore paths passed their controls.
items.mechanism: Move version/build constants to a light server module and export a dedicated backup entry; worker imports it directly and returns only result/error metadata.

evidence.label: Focused emitted worker and packaged verification

limits: The earlier 684,998→38,858-byte and 180.66→74.46-ms candidate probe is not the final emitted-build measurement; no final total-job speedup is claimed here.
Ordinary embedded-server queries still run synchronously in Electron main; backend isolation remains an evidence-led future decision.

items.title: Make attachment removal fair and promptly drain healthy backlog
items.summary: Schema v35 gives failed blob removals persistent eligibility/backoff so they cannot monopolize the first page.
items.before: One hundred permanently failing paths could keep a healthy 101st blob queued across restart; healthy pages waited for each 15-second timer.
items.after: Healthy removals continue on bounded later turns while individual failures back off, and permanent malformed names are visibly set aside.
items.mechanism: Stable due ordering uses queue time, attempts and next-attempt time; backoff grows through one minute, five, thirty and two hours. File bytes remain accounted until physical deletion succeeds.

evidence.label: Real healthy blob behind 100 failed removals and restart control

limits: This improves cleanup progress and correctness; no generic filesystem speedup is asserted.
Permanent failures remain visible and reserved storage is not falsely reclaimed.

items.title: Serve precompressed assets and reuse hashed browser files
items.summary: Build-time Brotli/gzip and immutable hashed-asset caching reduce repeated-host delivery work and cold bytes.
items.before: Hosts sent uncompressed client text and revalidated unchanged scripts with every visit; compressing at request time would add recurring CPU work.
items.after: Browsers negotiate prebuilt variants, hashed assets cache for a year, the page revalidates, and missing old chunks return explicit 404/no-store.
items.mechanism: Vite writes quality-11 Brotli/level-9 gzip sidecars once; @fastify/static serves variants with Vary. Integrity guards decode every copy and compare it to source.

evidence.label: REV-13 byte comparison and throttled browser experiment

metrics.label: Historical entry script + CSS, plain → Brotli
Cold first visible control, 200kB/s and 150ms RTT

limits: Median of seven throttled Chromium visits against earlier CLI output; later source changes alter byte totals.
Warm visible-control timing was effectively unchanged around 985 ms; API/attachment compression was not changed.

items.title: Prune dependency TypeScript from the desktop package
items.summary: Remove unused .ts/.cts/.mts files from packaged dependencies while preserving runtime JS, required metadata and licenses.
items.before: The clean desktop ASAR still carried TypeScript sources/declarations inside node_modules that Node never loads there.
items.after: Linux archive payload is smaller; both filtered and unfiltered packages retain working dependency/server/backup paths.
items.mechanism: Electron Builder excludes those extensions under node_modules; the archive guard rejects their accidental reintroduction.

evidence.label: F15 package and repeat runtime measurements

limits: Package-size gain only. Launch 1.42–1.46 s, hosting 1.48–1.53 s and memory ranges were indistinguishable between packages.
The excluded files were never read, so no startup or memory benefit is claimed.

items.title: Reuse verified task outputs and avoid unused installer stages
items.summary: Content-addressed Turbo reuse, bounded concurrency and installer-aware selection reduce redundant validation work.
items.before: Independent commands rebuilt web output, package worker pools overlapped, and every Windows runtime PR generated an installer that native tests did not use.
items.after: Task hashes cover complete source/config/test inputs; ordinary runtime PRs build unpacked Windows output while installer-sensitive changes retain NSIS.
items.mechanism: Cache task outputs separately from dependency/browser downloads; run cache/format/bundle/browser guards independently, limit task/Vitest concurrency and fail safe to full packaging when the base diff is unavailable.

evidence.label: Measured local reuse and historical hosted timings

metrics.label: Identical local repeat of all three task phases

limits: 1.09 s excludes install/cache transfer, formatting, browser setup and E2E; it is not total Actions duration.
Recorded 73–89 s prior installer stages describe expected avoided work, not a measured new remote saving.
Cache scope/permissions and correct invalidation remain essential; task caches are not a security boundary.

items.title: Separate lockfile dependency work from source-layer builds
items.summary: Container builds fetch pinned packages before copying source and install only the shipped dependency closure.
items.before: Any source change invalidated a stage that copied the whole repository before installation.
items.after: Source-only edits can reuse dependency fetch/install inputs; lock/toolchain/install-policy changes intentionally invalidate them.
items.mechanism: Multi-stage Node 24 image uses pnpm fetch, offline frozen filtered installation, stamped server/web builds and BuildKit Actions layer reuse. Final image copies only dist and runs as a non-root user.

evidence.label: REV-08 container reuse and independent validation

limits: No local before/after image timing is asserted; the documented Windows research environment lacked a usable Linux Docker engine.
Persistent-volume restart/socket and reuse smoke controls remain part of CI.

items.title: Bind tests and releases to matching source artifacts
items.summary: Stamped source-input identities, archive checks and repeatable release manifests prevent stale/unclean output from giving false test confidence.
items.before: Browser/native tests could launch leftover bundles, malformed identities could fail badly, and repeated release preparation could checksum old notes before rewriting them.
items.after: Tests reject missing/stale/malformed output with rebuild guidance; binary inputs are hashed exactly and release assets are a deliberate hash-bound set.
items.mechanism: One identity module supplies version/revision/dirty/input hashes to web/server/desktop, manifests and diagnostics; install gates inspect the actual app's profile report.

evidence.label: F05 implemented tooling versus genuine release/upgrade acceptance

limits: Assurance improvement, not a runtime speed claim.
A genuine upgrade from a published release and a real publication remain explicit acceptance work; unsigned packaging is not signed release proof.

items.title: Make performance decisions from successful reproducible work
items.summary: Server mixed-load and browser startup/image-scroll scripts record revision, fixture, host/runtime, samples and errors.
items.before: Earlier mixed probes could skip actual retention, accept incomplete replay and retain harness state that confounded memory/stalls.
items.after: F12 seeds exact expired data, verifies deletion and ordered replay/snapshot, bounds receipts/sockets and records offered/completed load.
items.mechanism: Workload scripts check correctness before/while timing; artifacts report latency distributions and scope rather than timing an error as successful work.
limits: These are measurement tools and baselines, not optimization speedups or declared capacity.
Historical mixed/cloud/headless results must not be treated as low-spec desktop-main/GPU acceptance; reference-hardware profiling remains open.

items.title: Make malformed query logging safe
items.summary: Invalid percent-encoded query names cannot terminate request logging.
items.before: A malformed query name could throw while being decoded by the redactor and escape the logging path.
items.after: Malformed names and their values are masked; the real child server keeps answering later requests.
items.mechanism: Catch query-name decoding failure before classifying sensitive parameters, mask both sides, and retain ordinary secret redaction.
limits: The regression proves the tested malformed-input boundary; no timing gain or natural crash frequency is claimed.

items.title: Keep one durable browser storage owner and recover conflicts
items.summary: IndexedDB failures remain visible/retryable, unfinished operations stay journaled and acknowledged operations are not reapplied, and multi-window recovery preserves local work.
items.before: Failed IndexedDB opening could silently switch to empty localStorage; optional BroadcastChannel absence could alter backend choice; older migration copies could overwrite private/local work.
items.after: Ownership is persisted before adoption, opening failure refuses alternate-backend writes, later calls can retry, and old conflicting drafts/outbox/privacy choices reconcile safely.
items.mechanism: Transactions serialize updates across independent contexts. Persistent operation IDs/tombstones prevent stale replay; legacy draft conflicts retain both texts, outbox removals remain removed and privacy reconciliation chooses the more private value. Storage-event/focus invalidation works without BroadcastChannel and carries no private payload.

evidence.label: Recovery, denied ownership and local-only watcher controls
Browser fault/retry, two-tab and browser-death validation scope

limits: Browser storage is not an OS power-loss guarantee.
Fresh profiles without IndexedDB can use localStorage until adoption; acknowledged IndexedDB ownership prevents later alternate fallback.
Q02/Q03/Q04/Q05 remain caller-level identity/preference/sign-in ordering findings; this backend fix does not close them.

items.title: Save the visible final composer text before native exit
items.summary: Desktop window close/quit waits for current UI text, pending local work and the native settings queue.
items.before: The last visible keystrokes could exist only in the renderer when native close destroyed the page.
items.after: Normal close captures current text and acknowledges persistence before destruction; failure keeps copying/retry/explicit unsaved exit available.
items.mechanism: Composer captures through layout cleanup, DraftPersistence drains restore/pending/failed/recovery work, preload sends a matching preparation reply, and main drains settings behind a window/request-bound handshake.

evidence.label: N03 exit behavior and harness corrections
Foreign/stale reply, failure and timeout controls

limits: Normal app close/quit verified on unpacked Windows output; forced process death, OS logoff and physical power loss are separate conditions.

items.title: Apply the latest mute intent when adopting a microphone
items.summary: Track replacement and both join entry points honor current acknowledged microphone preferences.
items.before: Held/recovered capture could adopt an older unmuted value; a join route could run before preference initialization settled.
items.after: Replacement tracks use the current desired-mute state; joins await the current initialization/save and unreadable preference state keeps capture muted with retry.
items.mechanism: Separate intent from the physical track. Preference generations fence late older reads against newer retries/saves and lifetime checks prevent canceled/unmounted join completion.

evidence.label: Held preference, muted join and entry-point regressions

limits: Synthetic media/held-capture controls do not establish physical unplug, real device selection or second-network calling acceptance.

items.title: Give each app form its own asynchronous lifetime
items.summary: A dismissed or replaced app form cannot receive an older submission's state or completion effects.
items.before: An old form's success, validation refusal or network failure could close or contaminate a replacement form.
items.after: Input, field errors and busy state belong to the active view; only that view's live request can update or close it.
items.mechanism: Key AppForm by view ID, guard component/submission lifetime, and fence WorkspaceClient submit/dismiss actions by the modal identity.
limits: This owns UI/modal completion; server concurrent submission and external-effect deduplication are separate N08 limits.

items.title: Strip action content from deleted and superseded message copies
items.summary: Deletion cleanup now removes interactive button labels, values and URLs from active tombstones and superseded replay events.
items.before: Text was cleaned while action payloads could retain user/app content after deletion or replacement.
items.after: Deleted rows and old replay copies carry no action payload; current live message buttons remain intact.
items.mechanism: Set actions to an empty array during soft deletion and replay redaction, then schema v37 cleans existing deleted/purged/superseded active database records.
limits: Active-record cleanup does not erase historical backups or freed SQLite disk pages.

items.title: Remove completed schedule content while retaining completion metadata
items.summary: Completed scheduled messages no longer keep a redundant text/file-ID copy in the schedule table.
items.before: An already-sent schedule still retained message text and attachment references after its delivery purpose ended.
items.after: Sent rows keep state/timing/completion identity without text or attachment IDs; queued unsent schedules retain what delivery requires.
items.mechanism: On completion write empty text and file_ids, and schema v37 migrates old sent rows under the same content-minimization policy.

evidence.label: Sent cleanup and queued preservation controls

limits: Removing duplicate schedule content is a privacy/storage-lifecycle fix; no measured database-size or throughput saving is claimed.
Historical backups and freed bytes remain outside this cleanup.

items.title: Exclude simultaneous duplicate app view submissions
items.summary: One app view can have only one callback in flight, with correction/retry available after it settles.
items.before: Concurrent requests for the same view could both reach the external application.
items.after: A second active submission gets 409 view_submitting, while later validation correction and deliberate transport retry still work.
items.mechanism: A per-view submitting Set is acquired before callback dispatch and released in finally; view/account ownership is validated independently.

evidence.label: N08 callback exclusion and retry limits
Concurrent, correction, independent-view and owner controls

limits: The Set prevents simultaneous dispatch, not exactly-once external business effects after an uncertain network reply. Apps should deduplicate by view ID.

items.title: Fence delayed app replace/delete directives to their origin revision
items.summary: An old response URL cannot replace/delete a message that disappeared or was changed since its callback origin.
items.before: Late directives could act on the message's newer state after an edit/deletion race.
items.after: Missing or changed origins make delayed replace/delete a no-op; an app can continue its own update chain through the same response URL.
items.mechanism: Hash origin text/editedAt/actions, compare before mutation and advance the shared origin revision after a valid self-update.

evidence.label: Delayed edit/delete and same-response chain controls

limits: The fingerprint covers the declared message fields; it is not a general cross-device revision protocol for all state.

items.title: Invalidate cached attachment bytes when a whole thread is retained away
items.summary: Retention removal reaches root and reply attachment ownership even after history eviction.
items.before: Cached blob URLs or held transfers could outlive a thread removed by retention because reply ownership was absent from the loaded history.
items.after: Root/reply bytes are canceled/released, a late transfer cannot reinstall them, and an active preview explains unavailability.
items.mechanism: File ownership includes threadRootId independent of loaded history. history.removed invalidates those owners; unknown-owner entries are conservatively revalidated on removal.
limits: Fresh server authorization already denied unavailable files; this fixes previously fetched local resources.
Previously downloaded/copied content cannot be retroactively unrevealed.

items.title: Preserve restored-copy holds despite damaged registry metadata
items.summary: Malformed display fields cannot cause a held restored workspace to be adopted into ordinary hosting.
items.before: A damaged name, port or timestamp could discard a registry row and lose the protection that kept a restored copy isolated.
items.after: Hold state survives recoverable display damage; uncertain held identities remain blocked while ordinary new-folder adoption stays supported.
items.mechanism: Parse safety-critical identity/hold metadata independently of optional presentation fields and fail closed when a held folder/identity cannot be established.
limits: This closes registry-adoption behavior; Q01's restore publication lock gap remains separate.

items.title: Retain connector/server ownership until cleanup actually succeeds
items.summary: Canceled/failed public setup cannot abandon handles that still need teardown.
items.before: An unsuccessful connector close could be treated as finished, allowing another route/access change while the old resource remained alive.
items.after: Failed cleanup stays pending, resource handles remain owned and reopening is gated until retry establishes cleanup.
items.mechanism: TunnelCleanupError carries the connector to the controller, including canceled/setup-failed handles and accidental-port isolated listeners. Cleanup waits are bounded and retryable; established close failures also mark pending cleanup.

evidence.label: N12 cleanup ownership and local limits

limits: Loopback/injected connector failures do not establish a real Cloudflare orphan frequency.
Q12 remains a separate main-adapter handle gap after listening; Q13 remains a pre-cleanup queue wait gap.

items.title: Keep history, attachment transfer and socket work bounded
items.summary: The architecture already caps retained page/cache work and avoids materializing whole file bodies during transfer.
items.before: Unbounded histories, independent duplicate file fetches or unchecked socket buffering would scale memory with session duration/load.
items.after: Timeline/thread windows hold 300 messages, inactive caches have 20 entries per category, idle blobs have a 32 MiB budget, body fetches have four slots and slow sockets use a 2 MiB queued-byte cutoff.
items.mechanism: LRU eviction protects active histories, file fetches deduplicate/cancel, image bodies load near the viewport, streaming server transfers preserve bounded body work, and reconnect uses durable replay/snapshot fallback.
limits: These are configured bounds, not comparative speed/memory measurements.
Active blobs, decoded pixels, complete account snapshots, aggregate connections and database/WAL/staging storage need separate budgets and profiling.

items.title: Contain background jobs and socket callback failures
items.summary: Actual scheduled/delivery/timer and Gateway callback faults no longer escape as unhandled process-ending work.
items.before: Read/rejection faults through native interval/immediate callbacks or socket heartbeat/message/close could terminate the host.
items.after: Queue failures retain durable rows and retry on later turns; unreadable session authorization sends no dependent frame and closes for recovery.
items.mechanism: Contain synchronous/asynchronous whole entry boundaries, report bounded queue failure metadata, deduplicate session checks within a batch and let explicit operational flush callers still learn that work failed.
limits: Fault injection establishes survival/correct recovery at these boundaries, not the frequency of real disk failures.
Durable jobs remain authoritative and no transaction failure is treated as accepted publication.

items.title: Keep accepted integration retry intent and healthy endpoint progress
items.summary: Durable repair intent respects admission limits/expiry, and independent endpoints refill freed delivery slots without a slow-peer barrier.
items.before: Retry could restore 1,500 rows into a 500-row ready queue; seven-day pruning could erase accepted waiting intent; one slow endpoint held back unrelated work.
items.after: A bounded ready queue promotes requested retries as space frees, retains requested intent through restart/expiry, and healthy endpoints advance while another remains held.
items.mechanism: Schema v36 records retry_requested; terminal-history pruning excludes accepted requested retry intent. The pump has at most ten concurrent operations and one per subscription, preserving per-subscription order.

evidence.label: REV-15 admission/pump mechanism and measured historical experiment
F04 expiry/restart and replay ordering contract

limits: Retry replay is ordered within its subset after already queued events, not globally inserted back into historical sequence order.
Uncertain external responses can repeat consumer effects; global integration count/byte budgets are still an operating-envelope decision.

items.title: Reconnect affected clients after failed access publication
items.summary: Committed revocation cannot leave the affected device indefinitely relying on stale cached access solely because its refresh notice failed.
items.before: Fresh HTTP correctly refused the removed user, but failed post-commit publication left its existing client showing old channel/history until manual reconnect.
items.after: Failure triggers resynchronization of the affected devices; handshake clears the revoked channel/history and preserves committed HTTP success.
items.mechanism: Target affected sessions for reconnect after access-state fan-out failure instead of rolling back a durable mutation or suppressing later events.

evidence.label: F06 implemented real WorkspaceClient regression and scope

limits: This removes previously fetched state after resynchronization; it does not undo data already downloaded or grant fresh unauthorized access.

items.title: Serialize local choice writes and stop queued work after destruction
items.summary: Pins, saved items, snooze and preference choices have one active local write, a coalesced latest choice and explicit client lifetime.
items.before: Reordered parallel writes or an old destroyed client's repair could overwrite its replacement client's newer choice.
items.after: Latest intent waits behind the in-flight request; destroy drops queued/repair work and refuses new writes.
items.mechanism: Per-item queues keep one request active, send the latest queued choice after it settles and guard corrections/echo reconciliation by client lifetime.

evidence.label: REV-11 serialized choices and destruction contract

limits: An already-delivered request cannot be recalled; cross-device ordering still needs a server revision contract.
Q09 shows Follow has a different unfixed ordering boundary and is not covered by this pin/save/snooze implementation.

items.title: Recover a failed renderer without stopping its host
items.summary: Electron retries a crashed/failed page within a bounded budget and restores its validated route/history context.
items.before: Renderer failures could leave a blank page; early retry restoration kept channel but lost Saved/thread/panel/query context.
items.after: Up to three failures in a minute reload automatically, followed by Try again/explicit action; main-side hosting remains alive and valid place state is handed back once.
items.mechanism: Separate renderer lifetime from native service ownership and retain a bounded trusted URL/history checkpoint outside renderer memory.

evidence.label: REV-09 and F08 packaged recovery behavior

limits: Recovered route state is validated against the account/workspace; it does not revive unauthorised local work.
Crash/power-loss durability remains subject to the separate acknowledged storage boundaries.

items.title: Keep exclusive restore ownership through folder publication
items.summary: Restore drops target ownership before swapping folders, allowing a concurrent real host to create an unrelated workspace at that path.
items.before: A controlled concurrent start causes restore publication to fail and leaves the original in a superseded folder.
items.after: Follow-up: retain exclusive admission throughout publication and rollback, using a stable lock identity outside the folder being renamed.
items.mechanism: Hold ownership until publication/rollback is complete; cover concurrent server start, two restores and failed rename without overwriting another target.

evidence.label: Q01 confirmed remaining finding and acceptance scope

limits: The original survives; the evidence does not prove irrecoverable deletion.
This is a local restore concurrency boundary, not a public remote restore endpoint.

items.title: Make first trusted-address registration atomic
items.summary: Two windows can each admit a distinct address after both read the same trusted-identity record as absent.
items.before: A second first-registration window can mount local-work consumers and read migrated text from the first address without approval.
items.after: Follow-up: use the storage owner's conditional initialization/atomic update so exactly one first address is admitted automatically.
items.mechanism: Replace the separate get/set absent check with an atomic owner operation; require deliberate approval for the losing distinct address before consumers mount.

evidence.label: Q02 confirmed remaining finding and acceptance scope

limits: Requires concurrent first registration; the ordinary second-address refusal control passes.
No alias approval bypass outside that race is established.

items.title: Fence stale notification preference replies
items.summary: Older initial-read/save completions can overwrite a newer private choice already received from another window.
items.before: Durable storage is private, while the active window returns to full previews after a delayed reply.
items.after: Follow-up: generation-fence replies against newer observed state and use an acknowledged current read if ordering is uncertain.
items.mechanism: Track the preference request/watch generation, including watches arriving before initial load; stale async replies must not restore less-private active state.

evidence.label: Q03 confirmed remaining finding and acceptance scope

limits: This is caller-level active-state ordering; N02's backend keeps the correct private durable value.
A passed diagnostic reproduces the failure and is not fix acceptance.

items.title: Keep unreadable composer preferences visible and safe
items.summary: A refused browser composer-preference read is treated as first-use absence.
items.before: A saved newline-on-Enter choice becomes Enter-to-send without an error and the actual composer invokes Send.
items.after: Follow-up: strict validated preference reads keep newline behavior on unreadability and expose a retry.
items.mechanism: Distinguish absent record from denied/corrupt read in the web adapter and composer preference owner; test held/refused reads and save acknowledgement.

evidence.label: Q04 confirmed remaining finding and acceptance scope

limits: The failure is conditional on record-specific unreadability.
The storage backend's owner/journal repair does not choose this caller's fallback UI behavior.

items.title: Merge saved sign-ins without reviving removals
items.summary: App writes a stale in-memory servers list as a whole.
items.before: A stale window switching workspaces can revive an explicitly forgotten sign-in or erase a sign-in newly stored by another window.
items.after: Follow-up: account-aware atomic add/remove/token changes plus open-window subscriptions preserve explicit removal intent.
items.mechanism: Use owner operations keyed by address/account and durable removals, then reconcile returned/current data without stale whole-list overwrite.

evidence.label: Q05 confirmed remaining finding and acceptance scope

limits: Uses actual App and IndexedDB with synthetic credentials; no token-revocation bypass is demonstrated.
Browser/Desktop caller policy needs coverage even though native settings serializes writes.

items.title: End saved-sign-in and password attempts when canceled
items.summary: Saved-sign-in and password completions can still invoke connected after their UI attempt is abandoned.
items.before: A canceled request or dismissed form can navigate into its old workspace after the reader moves on.
items.after: Follow-up: give these attempts cancellation/unmount identity guards like the existing address-probe control.
items.mechanism: Capture attempt generation/account identity; late success/failure cannot call connected or overwrite a newer attempt once abandoned.

evidence.label: Q06 confirmed remaining finding and acceptance scope

limits: Ordinary canceled address probes already ignore late success.
The reproduction is asynchronous UI ownership, not a server authentication defect.

items.title: Keep open search results synchronized with content removal/edit
items.summary: SearchDialog owns copied results independently of authoritative socket changes.
items.before: Deleted/retained or edited text remains in an already-open search until the reader repeats the query.
items.after: Follow-up: observe deletion/retention/edit/revocation and fence held result installation independent of loaded timeline history.
items.mechanism: Apply authoritative result invalidation or refresh to the search's copied rows and track request generation so late removed content cannot reinstall.

evidence.label: Q07 confirmed remaining finding and acceptance scope

limits: This is previously fetched text; fresh unauthorized retrieval is not established.
Preserve unrelated authorized result rows and normal paging/search access filters.

items.title: Refresh Pins independently of loaded timeline state
items.summary: Pins refresh reacts to loaded timeline pin data rather than every authoritative pin/deletion change.
items.before: A deleted pinned message remains in an open Pins panel when that channel timeline is not loaded.
items.after: Follow-up: subscribe to independent pin/removal changes and fence held panel results.
items.mechanism: Use server/socket message/pin invalidation scoped to the panel's channel, retaining loaded-history controls and explicit Refresh behavior.

evidence.label: Q08 confirmed remaining finding and acceptance scope

limits: Loaded-timeline and manual Refresh controls already clear the row.
This is stale previously fetched data, not a fresh access-grant bypass.

items.title: Order Follow/Unfollow by latest local intent
items.summary: Opposite Follow requests can race on the network/server.
items.before: Follow then Unfollow can finish followed when the older request reaches the server last; sequential calls finish unfollowed.
items.after: Follow-up: serialize/coalesce per-thread follow intent or use an explicit server revision contract.
items.mechanism: Keep one request active, send the latest queued choice, reconcile authoritative echoes and ensure failed older completion cannot roll back newer intent.

evidence.label: Q09 confirmed remaining finding and acceptance scope

limits: Actual HTTP/socket controls inject request ordering; natural frequency is unmeasured.
The completed pin/save/snooze queue does not cover Follow.

items.title: Identify unread rollback by request rather than cursor equality
items.summary: Repeated identical Mark unread actions share the same optimistic cursor value.
items.before: An older failure rolls local state back after a newer identical request succeeds, while SQLite remains unread.
items.after: Follow-up: associate rollback ownership with a request identity/generation and current authoritative echo.
items.mechanism: Only the still-owning failed request may restore its prior cursor; test repeated equal values, held failure, reconnect and multi-device updates.

evidence.label: Q10 confirmed remaining finding and acceptance scope

limits: The reproduced disagreement is local rollback; the server's stored unread state is correct.

items.title: Cancel Profile Message navigation ownership on dismissal
items.summary: A Profile Message action keeps its navigation completion alive after the dialog closes.
items.before: The old action opens its DM after the reader has navigated to another channel.
items.after: Follow-up: lifetime-guard Profile action completion and rejection, matching the working New message cancellation behavior.
items.mechanism: Dismiss/unmount increments action ownership; a late direct-message result must not navigate or contaminate the replacement view.

evidence.label: Q11 confirmed remaining finding and acceptance scope

limits: Real component/full WorkspaceScreen control establishes the action boundary; ordinary New message already has a dismissal guard.

items.title: Close a created listener when post-start invite setup fails
items.summary: Main's startup adapter starts listening before configured invite policy is enforced.
items.before: A failed policy write loses the server handle before returning it to the controller; shutdown reports success while health still answers and ownership remains locked.
items.after: Follow-up: retain the newly created server in a protected try/finally until startup either transfers ownership or closes it.
items.mechanism: Acquire the handle immediately after create/listen, run policy checks inside a cleanup-protected block and transfer it to the controller only after complete success.

evidence.label: Q12 confirmed remaining finding and acceptance scope

limits: Actual extracted startup callback, real SQLite write-refusing trigger and loopback listener establish the controlled failure.
This is adjacent to N12's controller/connector fixes, which remain in place.

items.title: Bound shutdown waiting before it reaches cleanup
items.summary: Shutdown joins the hosting operation queue behind an outstanding backup.
items.before: A held backup leaves the listener running beyond six injected cleanup deadline intervals because timed cleanup has not begun.
items.after: Follow-up: define bounded cancellation/settlement for preceding queued/in-flight work while retaining resource ownership.
items.mechanism: Start an overall shutdown policy before queue wait, distinguish accepted durable work from abortable work and retain handles until each cancellation/cleanup outcome is established.

evidence.label: Q13 confirmed remaining finding and acceptance scope

limits: A held adapter proves queue behavior; it does not establish a real blocked network-share backup or observed native exit hang.
A timeout must not abandon the worker/server resource or silently claim unfinished backup success.
